title: Capitol Reef National Park: Monsoon Season & Flash Floods
summary: Heavy rains can cause sudden flooding, especially in canyons and washes. Do not drive or hike through flood waters. Get to high ground and wait for floods to subside. Some roads may close temporarily; closures are posted at the visitor center.

title: Capitol Reef National Park: Elevated E. Coli levels - Fremont River and Sulphur Creek
summary: Recent water quality testing shows elevated E. coli levels in the Fremont River and Sulphur Creek. A warning advisory has been issued by the Utah DEQ. Use caution if entering the water. Do not get water in your mouth, do not swim. Wash hands with soap and water.

title: FUL-Field Staff Law Enforcement Ranger — Bureau of Land Management
summary: You will serve as a FUL-Field Staff Law Enforcement Ranger for the Bureau of Land Management Green River District. The Law Enforcement Ranger serves as a uniformed representative who enforces federal laws and regulations on public lands, including supporting agency presence in the community. You may be required to work on-call, evenings, weekends, holidays, overtime and shift work. · $58,771–$84,5

title: Capitol Reef National Park
summary: Located in south-central Utah in the heart of red rock country, Capitol Reef National Park is a hidden treasure filled with cliffs, canyons, domes, and bridges in the Waterpocket Fold, a geologic monocline (a wrinkle on the earth) extending almost 100 miles.
